class.name: SnowClimate
class.brief_description: A place's winter weather, and the snowpack a season of it leaves on the terrain.
class.description: A recipe for the weather of a place and, once [method SnowCover3D.bake_climate] has run a season of it over the terrain, the snowpack that season left: snow water, density, liquid water and albedo per cell, and the cornices on lee crests. Assign it to [member SnowCover3D.climate] and the cover keeps a coarse world tier of snow over the whole baked square, carries it on with the weather, seeds the near square from it and draws it on materials beyond the near square. The weather is a daily stochastic generator in the manner of WGEN (Richardson 1981): wet and dry days from a two-state Markov chain ([member wet_after_dry], [member wet_after_wet]), exponential amounts on wet days, the day's mean temperature a seasonal harmonic between [member january_temperature] and [member july_temperature] plus a persistent residual, a daily cycle on top, a Weibull wind speed around a prevailing direction, stormier on wet days. The sun follows [member latitude] and the date; clouds dim it (Kasten and Czeplak 1980). The bake steps the same snowpack model as [SnowCover3D]: rain or snow by temperature (Jennings et al. 2018), more precipitation higher up ([member precipitation_gradient]), settling, melt by temperature and sun on each slope, SnowSlide, and wind drift by Winstral's Sx, so a mountain gets a snow line, shaded faces that keep their snow, sunny faces that lose it and loaded lee slopes.

method.name: clear_result
method.description: Forgets the baked snowpack, keeping the recipe.

method.name: is_baked
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] once a bake has stored a snowpack.

method.name: sample_days
method.description: Runs the weather generator from its seed for [param days] days and returns four floats a day: mean temperature at [member base_height] (C), water (mm), mean wind speed (m/s) and [code]1[/code] for a wet day. For checks and tuning.

method.name: seasonal_lapse_rate
method.description: The temperature lapse rate in C/km on a day of the year, a harmonic between the [member recipe]'s [member ClimateRecipe.lapse_rate_january] and [member ClimateRecipe.lapse_rate_july]. Returns [param default] without a recipe. [method SnowCover3D.bake_climate] uses it each day.

method.name: seasonal_temperature
method.description: The seasonal mean temperature at [member base_height] on a day of the year, coldest in late January.

method.name: sun_direction
method.description: The direction toward the sun at [member latitude] on a day of the year and a local solar hour: x east, y up, z south (north is -z). Below the horizon when y is negative.

method.name: wet_day_amount
method.description: The mean water of a wet day, in mm, on a day of the year. With a [member recipe], the month's share of [member ClimateRecipe.precipitation] (by [member ClimateRecipe.precipitation_seasonality] and [member ClimateRecipe.precipitation_peak_month]) over the Markov chain's share of wet days; without one, [member wet_day_precipitation].

The terrain's climate, the same [ClimateRecipe] its [TerrainGenerator3D] rivers and [TerrainDataMap3D] climate maps use. When set, [method start_weather] (and so every bake) takes from it [member latitude], [member base_height] (its reference height), [member january_temperature], [member july_temperature], [member temperature_variability] (its daily temperature spread), [member prevailing_wind_from], [member wind_spread] and the wet-day wind (so [member wind_speed] becomes its wind speed over [member storm_wind_factor]); each month's wet-day amount follows its precipitation and seasonality ([method wet_day_amount]); the bake's lapse rate follows its winter and summer values ([method seasonal_lapse_rate]). The wet and dry day chain and [member daily_range] stay this resource's. Point [member SnowCover3D.climate_map] at the data map for its orographic precipitation too.
